transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-19 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recorded: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (HelioDynamics Head of ML), Connor Li (Infra), Priya Nair (Security)

Summary:
HelioDynamics is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a mixed workload (real-time chat + nightly batch embeddings). Primary concerns: guaranteed throughput during spikes, tenant isolation for multi-product teams, VPC/KMS integration, and a clean fallback path to hosted models to avoid downtime. They asked for a surge simulation and reserved SKU pricing.

Topics covered:
- Current infra and signal patterns (p50/p95/p99)
- Reserved GPU sizing and warm-pool strategies
- Isolation options: node fencing, tenant pinning, and private deployment tradeoffs
- Encryption/KMS and audit log requirements
- Fallbacks to lower-cost model variants and routing policies
- Pilot/surge simulation next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, good afternoon — thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:10] Sofia (Helio): Hi, Sofia here, I run ML. We are looking to move heavier inference for our recommendations and chat use cases to dedicated infra.
[00:18] Connor: Connor, infra, I'll be owning the integration and runbooks.
[00:21] Priya: Priya, security, mainly here for KMS and compliance gating.
[00:26] Jon (Redwood SE): Jon Ortiz, SE — I'll run through sizing and simulations.
[00:30] Maya: Cool. High level — we heard you have both latency sensitive requests and big nightly embedding batches. Can you paint the traffic shape?
[00:40] Sofia: Yeah, so day: real-time chat, about 120 TPS p50 is like 40-50ms on our current smaller model, p99 can spike to 700ms during peak because of queuing. Night: embeddings batches, up to 40k requests/hour but not latency sensitive. We also do A/B experiments which temporarily double traffic for short windows.
[01:05] Jon: Okay that helps. Are you looking for reserved nodes to own capacity or a hybrid where you have reserved but allow burst onto host?
[01:12] Connor: We want guaranteed capacity for chat; embeddings can go to burst or hosted. Main ask: when we hit 2–3x traffic for short windows (1–15 minutes) the chat must not degrade beyond 10% p99 increase.
[01:25] Maya: Got it. That points to a warm-pool + prewarm strategy plus routing policy to fall back to lighter model variants when necessary.
[01:35] Sofia: Can you explain warm-pool? We saw the term in docs but unclear on cold-starts and KV cache behavior.
[01:42] Jon: Sure — warm-pool are reserved instances kept in a pre-initialized state (weights loaded, KV cache primed for recent prefixes if applicable). It reduces first-token latency during burst. The KV cache is per-request session, so we do prefix caching; sometimes transcripts refer to it as K V cash in speech.
[01:58] Connor: Are we able to pin certain tenants to isolated nodes? We have three product teams and want crash isolation.
[02:06] Jon: Yes, dedicated supports node-level tenant fencing. Options: soft multi-tenant on reserved pool with tenant quotas, or hard fencing where a node is dedicated to a tenant. Hard fencing gives stronger blast radius control but less statistical multiplexing.
[02:24] Priya: From security side, we need KMS integration (HSM-backed preferred), audit logs for per-request data access, and SOC2 docs. Also, data residency for EU users.
[02:36] Maya: We can integrate with customer-managed KMS, HSM options are part of our Private offering but Redwood Dedicated supports customer KMS via key wrapping and audit export. SOC2 report is available — we'll share.
[02:48] Sofia: If we do dedicated in region A and some users in EU, does Redwood replicate traffic or require separate clusters?
[02:55] Jon: You can provision dedicated pools per region. Smart routing can send EU traffic to EU pool to satisfy residency. There is also a cross-region fallback but that needs compliance signoff.
[03:08] Connor: On preemption: if we reserve GPUs, what are eviction risks? We heard about spot preempts elsewhere.
[03:15] Jon: Reserved capacity in Redwood Dedicated are committed — no preemption for reserved nodes. There are warm-pool ephemeral nodes for burst which may be subject to eviction depending on underlying cloud signals, but we surface that in SLAs and provide fallback to hosted model variants.
[03:30] Sofia: Can you quantify how many GPUs for our baseline? Our model is a ~13B transformer running fp16 on A100-ish hardware.
[03:38] Jon: For real-time low-latency, a common starting point is 2–3 GPUs per 1000 concurrent chat sessions depending on sequence length. For 120 TPS with average concurrency ~120–240 depending on prompt length — rough ballpark would be a pool of 4 GPUs for baseline, plus a warm-pool of 2 GPUs to cover 2x spikes. We'll confirm with exact model perf test.
[04:00] Connor: That seems small; our current infra uses bigger headroom. We want to run a throughput test.
[04:06] Jon: Absolutely — we'll run a 2hr surge sim with your traces to validate. We'll also run quantized model variant tests; quantization can reduce GPU footprint by ~1.5–2x but might have small delta in quality.
[04:22] Priya: About logs and PII: we only want metadata and need sensitive fields redacted before any logs leave our VPC. Is that supported?
[04:31] Maya: For Private deployments we can guarantee no egress. For Dedicated we support in-transit encryption and can configure redaction rules and limited audit exports; we'll map options for you.
[04:42] Sofia: Is there a quick fallback policy if the reserved pool hits capacity? Prefer not to degrade chat quality but we'd accept temporarily routing to a lighter model.
[04:50] Jon: We recommend a staged fallback: 1) spill to warm-pool; 2) if still saturated, route a percentage of requests to quantized/lighter model variant; 3) if still saturated, route non-user-facing traffic to hosted endpoints or queue. These are policy configurable per route.
[05:12] Connor: How do you measure the 10% p99 threshold — do you have canarying that will detect regressions?
[05:20] Jon: Yes, the Redwood Console exposes per-route p50/p95/p99 and token-level latency. We can setup evals with your golden prompts to detect quality regressions when switching variants.
[05:32] Sofia: What's the expected lead time to provision a reserved pool? We are conscious of procurement windows.
[05:38] Maya: For standard reserved pools in common regions it's typically 2–4 weeks from contract signature. For private/on-prem it's longer, 8–12 weeks depending on network setups and approvals.
[05:50] Priya: For contract: we need data processing addendum and clarity on incident response SLAs.
[05:56] Maya: We'll include DPA and an SLA addendum draft. Incident response times vary by support tier; we'll flag enterprise SLA options in the pricing doc.
[06:07] Sofia: Could we see a failure mode example? Like RAID node failure and how failover happens for active KV cache sessions?
[06:15] Jon: Sure — if a node fails active KV cache is lost for sessions tied to that node; we have session migration where subsequent requests can be served from a fallback model without cached prefixes which can increase latency. For critical sessions we recommend sticky routing to warm nodes and periodic checkpointing of state to reduce blast. There is some clarity tradeoff.
[06:40] Connor: What about billing during burst? If we have reserved 4 GPUs and burst onto 2 ephemeral ones, how is that priced?
[06:48] Maya: Reserved tier has flat monthly commit for the reserved pool; ephemeral burst is billed at a higher per-minute rate. We can model blended unit economics for your traffic profile to show net cost.
[06:58] Sofia: We'd like an example runbook for an unexpected 5x spike during business hours. Can Redwood auto-scale or we need manual ops?
[07:07] Jon: We support autoscaling policies but with reserved pools you usually configure a guarded burst: warm-pool prewarm and autoscale to ephemeral burst up to a hard cap. You can set auto-fallback thresholds to avoid unbounded cost. For mission-critical features we advise a canary-based rollout for models and a synthetic traffic monitor to pre-trigger scale.
[07:30] Sofia: Ok, on region failover — if a region A goes down, is there automatic failover to region B?
[07:36] Jon: Automatic failover exists but it must be enabled and you pay cross-region egress. Also data residency rules could prohibit it. It's often manual with an automated playbook for safety.
[07:49] Priya: Concerning encryption at rest — we need to know if model artifacts are encrypted with customer key.
[07:55] Maya: Model artifacts on Dedicated can be encrypted with CMKs via KMS; Private deployments can use HSM-backed KMS for additional assurance. We'll capture required specifics in the compliance packet.
[08:05] Connor: For the surge sim — what inputs do you need from us?
[08:09] Jon: Ideally: 1) 1 week of request traces with timestamps and tokens/sequence lengths, 2) representative prompts and golden responses, 3) desired SLA targets and which routes are critical.
[08:20] Connor: We'll anonymize traces and remove PII. We'll also include sticky session patterns.
[08:25] Sofia: About model variance — if we route to a quantized variant, how do you monitor for quality slip?
[08:31] Jon: Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals against golden prompts and trigger alerts when metric drift exceeds thresholds. We also support shadow traffic testing to compare outputs without impacting users.
[08:45] Maya: Quick question for ordering: do you expect to start with a pilot or go straight to full reserved?
[08:50] Sofia: Pilot — we want a week-long pilot with the chat route and a short SLO target. If it hits, we expand. Procurement timeline might be 3–4 weeks post-pilot.
[08:59] Maya: Great. We'll propose a pilot scope — small reserved pool + burst sim.
[09:05] Priya: Regarding audit trails — do you provide per-token audit logs or summaries? We prefer summaries for sensitive data.
[09:12] Jon: We can emit structured logs with sampling and redaction rules; per-token logs can be available but typically customers choose sampled aggregated telemetry.
[09:22] Sofia: For warm-pool cost, can you show a comparison: bigger reserved vs more frequent burst? I want to see cost tradeoffs for steady vs spiky traffic.
[09:30] Maya: We'll include a cost bake-off with your traces in the pricing sheet. It will show dollars per 1000 requests across scenarios.
[09:38] Connor: Any network topology constraints — we have strict VPC peering rules and private subnets.
[09:43] Jon: Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink; we will need CIDR ranges and firewall rules. For Private on-prem we'll provide an appliance that connects via a vetted tunnel.
[09:58] Priya: Are there restrictions on bringing our own models? We have internal models not open-sourced.
[10:03] Jon: Customers can bring models; we support model onboarding with a compatibility test. For private deployments you can keep models inside your network. For hosted Dedicated we require model artifacts to be uploaded to a secured storage location; access controls apply.
[10:18] Sofia: One more question: how do you handle gradual rollouts and canarying in Dedicated?
[10:24] Jon: We offer canary routing policies — route X% to new version, auto-promote based on eval signals or manual. You can do A/B experiments and Redwood Console will surface per-variant metrics.
[10:37] Maya: Let's go through the agreed immediate next steps — I'll read them out and anyone can correct.
[10:41] Maya: Redwood to share pricing + reserved SKUs and a draft DPA by Thursday 2026-01-22.
[10:48] Sofia: Confirmed.
[10:49] Maya: HelioDynamics to share anonymized traces and golden prompts by Wednesday 2026-01-21.
[10:55] Connor: Yep, we'll do that.
[10:57] Maya: Jon to schedule a 2hr surge simulation the week of Jan 26 after traces are in.
[11:02] Jon: I'll send a calendar invite and prep checklist.
[11:06] Priya: We'll review the SOC2 + KMS docs once you send them.
[11:10] Maya: Perfect. Any final questions?
[11:15] Sofia: Just one — can Redwood provide a sample SLA for sustained outages?
[11:19] Maya: Yes, included in the enterprise SLA packet — we'll append examples.
[11:23] Jon: Also, we'll include a sample runbook for a 5x spike and the expected latency profile.
[11:30] Sofia: Great, thanks everyone.
[11:32] Connor: Thanks all.
[11:33] Priya: Thank you.
[11:35] Maya: End call.

Post-call notes:
- SE flagged need to test model perf on A100 and an NVMesh-backed storage path; Jon will coordinate infra for test.
- Pricing to include blended cost model and reserved vs burst comparison; include savings if quantized model is acceptable.
- Compliance packet to include DPA, SOC2, KMS/HSM options, and audit log capabilities.
